MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with lymph node involvement
Specimen Type: Tissue biopsy
Tumor Content: 25%

TEST PERFORMED
Comprehensive Cancer Panel - DNA and RNA Analysis

METHODOLOGY
DNA Panel: Amplicon-based next-generation sequencing of 57 cancer-related genes using PCR amplification. Sequencing performed on Illumina platform with dual variant calling algorithms. The assay detects single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions with ≥2.5% allele frequency with a minimum of 15 supporting reads.

RNA Panel: Fusion and expression analysis attempted but failed due to insufficient RNA quality.

Genes Analyzed (DNA Panel): ABL1, AKT1, ALK, APC, ATM, BRAF, CDH1, CDKN2A, CSF1R, CTNNB1, EGFR, ERBB2, ERBB4, EZH2, FBXW7, FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, FLT3, GNA11, GNAQ, GNAS, HNF1A, HRAS, IDH1, IDH2, JAK2, JAK3, KDR, KIT, KRAS, MET, MLH1, MPL, NOTCH1, NPM1, NRAS, PDGFRA, PIK3CA, PTEN, PTPN11, RB1, RET, SMAD4, SMARCB1, SMO, SRC, STK11, TP53, TSC1, VHL, and others.

RESULTS

DNA ANALYSIS - VARIANTS DETECTED:

KRAS (NM_033360.3)
Variant: c.35G>C, p.Gly12Ala
Variant Allele Frequency: 32%
Clinical Significance: Pathogenic

DNA ANALYSIS - GENES WITH NO REPORTABLE VARIANTS:

EGFR: No variants detected in exons 18-21 (including codons 719, 746-750, 768, 790, 858, 861)
BRAF: No variants detected in codons 443-474 and 582-608 (including V600)

STRUCTURAL VARIANT ANALYSIS:
Analysis failed due to technical limitations

RNA ANALYSIS:
Failed - Insufficient RNA quality

INTERPRETATION

The KRAS p.Gly12Ala variant detected at 32% allele frequency is a well-characterized oncogenic mutation commonly found in NSCLC. This variant results in constitutive activation of the RAS signaling pathway.

Clinical Implications:
- KRAS mutations predict decreased sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in NSCLC
- Patients with KRAS mutations are unlikely to benefit from EGFR inhibitor therapy (erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, osimertinib)
- KRAS G12 mutations also predict lack of response to MEK inhibitors and BRAF inhibitors
- Due to RNA panel failure, candidacy for ALK, ROS1, RET, MET, and NTRK fusion-targeted therapies could not be determined

RECOMMENDATIONS

Based on the molecular findings:
- Patient is unlikely to benefit from targeted therapies against EGFR, MEK, or BRAF
- Standard chemotherapy or immunotherapy approaches should be considered
- Consider repeat biopsy for RNA fusion analysis if clinically indicated

ASSAY LIMITATIONS
- This assay detects variants with allele frequencies ≥2.5%
- Structural variants and gene fusions require adequate RNA quality
- Not all exons of all genes are covered
- Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical and pathological findings

Electronically signed by: Dr. [redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
